chapter_title: Concerning the Four Works of the Ambassador
chapter_note: This chapter is essentially a compact, systematic fourfold exposition (image; doors of firmaments; purification/release of light; manifestation of the light ship and living soul). The only clearly later material is the brief dialogue/frame attribution in ¶1 (“Once again the enlightener speaks:”), which wraps an otherwise core, impersonal cosmological statement.

paragraphs.core_text: At the time when the Ambassador displayed his image, four great works were revealed that are very excellent and outstanding.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed hagiographic/dialogue attribution: “Once again the enlightener speaks:” (frame formula identifying the speaker).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening frame formula with a named speaker (“the enlightener”) is characteristic of the Kephalaia’s editorial/hagiographic apparatus; the remaining clause shifts to impersonal, structural cosmological exposition (a numbered set of “four works”).

paragraphs.core_text: The first is his image that he displayed in a glorious image.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered, impersonal listing of salvific/cosmic mechanisms (the Ambassador’s image) without audience address, citation, or institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is all the doors of the firmaments that were opened at that time. They open [...] and shut behind him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the systematic fourfold sequence; purely cosmological architecture (“doors of the firmaments”), with no polemical or pastoral extension.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the light and the releasing that was purified by his image. That light is more than the light that he shall [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Process-mechanistic, cosmological purification language (“light,” “releasing,” “purified”) anchored to the Ambassador’s image; no institutional referent despite a slight comparative turn.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth: He has [made apparent], by the perfection of people, his light ship. He has [...] the living soul that shone forth in perfection and fullness over the worlds of enmity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the fourfold structure with core Manichaean cosmological entities/processes (“light ship,” “living soul,” “worlds of enmity”). The phrasing remains explanatory rather than hortatory; no explicit contemporary-world identification.
